It's an easy model to fall into. The file name reads like "the production copy". The project template's
section almost line for line, which looks like a full copy with a few keys removed. And for simple values, "replaced" and "overridden" look identical: set
in the production file and production uses that host either way.

The difference only shows up for the keys the environment file doesn't mention. Under replacement they'd vanish; in reality they stay. The wrong model also breeds a defensive habit: copying the whole base file into every environment file "to be safe". It protects nothing, because the keys still merge, and it leaves two copies of each setting to drift apart.

blocks.title: Shorter or empty lists don't shrink anything

content.text: An environment file can't shorten an array from a lower layer. A one-item list overrides index 0 only, and an empty list overrides nothing at all. A security-relevant list in
, such as CORS origins, allowed hosts or admin emails, leaks its extra items into every environment that sets a shorter one.
